title: Make an independent copy
summary: A copy owns separate data. It is useful when changing a result must not change the original array.
introduction: A copy owns separate data. It is useful when changing a result must not change the original array. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A copy owns separate data. It is useful when changing a result must not change the original array.

blocks.code:
import numpy as np

original = np.array([1, 2, 3])
copy = original.copy()
copy[0] = 99
print(original.tolist())
blocks.title: Make an independent copy

blocks.text: The original remains [1, 2, 3]. copy[0] changes only the copied data.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Compare this with a basic slice view in a separate experiment.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Assigning copy = original only gives the same array another name.
For more detail later, use this [NumPy further reading](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/absolute_beginners.html).
